note.note:
Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS); current episode of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic pain with pink-tinged urine—concern for acute uncomplicated cystitis. No chronic cardiometabolic conditions recorded.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  “No” to bladder/kidney problems; other family history not recorded.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Combined oral contraceptive pill – dose/route/frequency not documented; Mebeverine – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Sexually active with long-term boyfriend; unprotected intercourse ~1 week ago; on combined OCP; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago; no abnormal vaginal discharge; pregnancy considered unlikely but not ruled out if symptoms persist.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Occasional social alcohol use; non-smoker; first-time cannabis use 1.5 weeks ago; no ongoing illicit drug use planned. Physical activity and diet not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Not recorded.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Not recorded.  
- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:  University student (English), living in halls with a flat-mate; family lives nearby and is supportive; financial/housing stressors not reported.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:  Not recorded (telephone consult).  
- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:  Not recorded.  
- Ear exam including otoscopy:  Not recorded.  
- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:  Not recorded.  
- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:  Planned—mid-stream urine to be collected and sent for dipstick/culture; results pending.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Blood tests: fasting glucose and lipids preferred; HbA1c if diabetes present/suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Renal function and liver function tests if clinically indicated:  Not recorded.  
- ECG if cardiac risk factors present or baseline:  Not recorded.  
- Cervical screening if eligible and due:  Not recorded.  
- Mammography if eligible and not up to date:  Not applicable (age 19).  
- Faecal occult blood test if due:  Not applicable (age 19).  
- Bone density (DEXA) if osteoporosis risk present:  Not applicable (age 19).

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 19-year-old woman with 6-7 days of dysuria, urinary frequency, suprapubic ache, and pink-tinged urine; no fever, flank pain, nausea, or vomiting. Past IBS; on OCP and Mebeverine; allergic to Clindamycin.

Working diagnosis: Acute uncomplicated cystitis (bacterial UTI) – high likelihood given classic symptom triad and absence of systemic features. 

Supporting DDx information: DDx model also ranks acute uncomplicated cystitis as “High” probability.  

Considerations:  
• Chlamydial or gonococcal urethritis/cervicitis – medium likelihood due to unprotected sex; will consider if culture negative or persistent symptoms.  
• Distal ureteric/bladder calculus – low–medium likelihood; less typical presentation.  

Management:  
• Empirical oral antibiotics: options discussed—Nitrofurantoin 3-day course or Trimethoprim (dose not documented).  
• Mid-stream urine sample to be dropped at practice for dipstick and culture; adjust antibiotics per sensitivities.  
• Hydration advice; symptomatic relief with paracetamol.  
• Safety-net: seek review if fever, back pain, vomiting, or no improvement within one week.  
• Pregnancy test to be considered if symptoms persist despite treatment.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed maintaining hydration; advised against further cannabis use; counselled on safe sexual practices and potential condom use to reduce STI risk.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Relief of urinary symptoms and return to normal university activities.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not applicable.  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Not indicated today.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Telephone or face-to-face review after urine culture or sooner if symptoms worsen; results notification planned.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded.  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not indicated.  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded.  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded.  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded.  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Acute uncomplicated cystitis – High likelihood: classic dysuria, frequency, suprapubic ache, microhematuria, no systemic signs.  
2. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis or cervicitis – Medium likelihood: recent unprotected intercourse; STI can mimic cystitis; absent vaginal discharge lowers probability.  
3. Distal ureteric/bladder stone – Low-Medium likelihood: hematuria and irritative voiding possible, but lacks colicky flank pain and uncommon at age 19.

Quality checks

● Missing but clinically expected elements: vitals, BMI, immunisation review, cervical screening status, mental health screening, substance use risk assessment depth.  
● Internal conflicts: none noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality notes: clear audio; purely telephone consultation—no physical exam or vitals obtained.
